beats.care: Cooking in a shared flat or hostel? You can buy up to 5 kg each at Amutham and cooperative stores.
beats.what: Ministers P Venkataramanan and V Gandhiraj launched ₹30/kg fine rice on Saturday at 11 Amutham and 19 cooperative stores in Chennai.
beats.why: The government wants to ease grocery bills. It plans to sell toor dal at ₹130 a kg too, against ₹170–190 outside.

cards.body: Each consumer or family member can buy up to 5 kg of the ₹30 rice.
cards.caption: limit per consumer

cards.body: Toor dal sells for ₹170–190 a kg in the open market. The state is looking at selling it for ₹130 at cooperative stores, with a launch expected within days.
cards.title: Dal next?

opts: To sell at a lower price than the open market
cards.q: Why does the state sell rice through its own cooperative stores?
cards.why: Selling bought stock through state stores lets it offer rice and dal below open-market prices.

cover.label: fine rice at Chennai co-op stores

hook: Where can you buy *fine rice for ₹30 a kg* in Chennai?

learn.t: The state bought 25,000 tonnes of rice to sell through 250 cooperative stores across Tamil Nadu.

sources.name: DT Next
sources.title: Fine rice at Rs 30/kg launched in 30 locations in Chennai

tldr: Tamil Nadu has started selling fine-quality rice at ₹30 a kg at 30 outlets in Chennai, with a 5 kg limit per person.
watch: The scheme was set to extend beyond Chennai to cooperative stores statewide from Sunday, October 18.
